review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Increasing in the knowledge of God.

elsewhere.note: I stir up your sincere mind by reminder.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Whom I have begotten in my bonds.

My defense to those who examine me.

Making himself equal with God.

elsewhere.note: He didn't consider equality with God a thing to be grasped.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

That our boasting may not be in vain.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Every tongue will confess to God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Dung, garbage, scraps thrown to the dogs, a vulgar word. In 3:8, Paul counts all his credentials "nothing but refuse" compared with knowing Christ. It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: I count them nothing but refuse.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Something suffered, a suffering or a passion. In 3:10, Paul wants to share "the fellowship of his sufferings." In Romans 8:18, "the sufferings of this present time" are not worth comparing with the glory.

elsewhere.note: The sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing.
The sufferings of Christ abound to us.
Through sufferings.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To be shaped into the same form as something. In 3:10, Paul wants to be "conformed to his death." It appears only here; the related adjective symmorphos is in 3:21 and Romans 8:29.

elsewhere.note: Becoming conformed to his death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To come to a destination, to arrive or reach. In 3:11, "if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead." In Ephesians 4:13, "until we all attain to the unity of the faith."

elsewhere.note: He came to Derbe and Lystra.
Our twelve tribes hope to attain.
Until we all attain to the unity of the faith.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To bring to the end or goal, to make complete. In 3:12, Paul says he is not "already made perfect" but presses on. Jesus said on the cross, "It is finished" (a related word, John 19:30).

elsewhere.note: On the third day I complete my work.
That they may be perfected into one.
To make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To strain toward something, as a runner stretches toward the finish line. In 3:13, "stretching forward to the things which are before." It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: Stretching forward to the things which are before.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A mark to aim at, a goal or target (from which we get "scope"). In 3:14, "I press on toward the goal for the prize." It appears only here.

elsewhere.note: I press on toward the goal.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Only one receives the prize.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A call, an invitation, or a vocation. In 3:14, "the upward call of God in Christ Jesus." In 1 Corinthians 1:26, Paul says to "consider your calling."

elsewhere.note: The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
Consider your calling, brothers.
In one hope of your calling.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

range.note: Another who follows the same model.

elsewhere.note: Brothers, be imitators together of me.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction.
Vessels of wrath fitted for destruction.
The day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: They serve their own belly.
Even from his mother's womb.
Foods for the belly.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Begin with shame to take the lowest place.
Endured the cross, despising shame.
Foaming out their own shame.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: If I told you earthly things.
Heavenly bodies and earthly bodies.
This wisdom is earthly.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The community of citizens, a colony or commonwealth, or the citizenship itself (from politēs, "citizen"). In 3:20, "our citizenship is in heaven." In Philippi, a Roman colony, the metaphor would resonate: the colony's citizens were a piece of Rome abroad.

elsewhere.note: Our citizenship is in heaven.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: He has looked at the humble state of his servant.
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away.
The rich in his humiliation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: To be conformed to the image of his Son.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

range.note: One who pulls the same load.

elsewhere.note: Yes, I ask you also, true yokefellow, help these women.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

To be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
The wisdom from above is gentle.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Summer is near.
The time is near.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Pilate decided that what they asked for should be done.
We know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Deacons must be reverent.

Older men should be temperate, reverent.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Whatever things are of good report.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Who called us by his own glory and virtue.
Add to your faith virtue.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

To the praise of the glory of his grace.
Might be found to result in praise.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry.

elsewhere.note: Don't participate in the unfruitful works of darkness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Through death he might destroy him who had the power of death.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

That petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me.

Let them first learn to show piety at home.

Working in us that which is well-pleasing in his sight.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The riches of his goodness and forbearance.

We are the circumcision, who worship by the Spirit of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.

The fruit of the Spirit.

Your zeal for me.
As to zeal, a persecutor of the church.

Pursue hospitality.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God.

We know the Spirit of truth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.
I am the resurrection and the life.

This is the first resurrection.

Solid food is for the mature.
Let endurance finish its work, that you may be complete.

To be of the same mind in the Lord.

Our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Who will transform the body of our humiliation.

With all power and signs.

Be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution.

As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah.
